<timestamp>Thursday, Nov 19, 2026, 3:45 PM (UTC-8)</timestamp>
<user_query>
my partner built all the bots himself on his personal account, how does he actually connect his bots
</user_query>
I'll look through the project and how bots are wired so I can explain how a personal-account bot actually connects.

The bots stay on his Grok account. Waypoint never hosts them. They connect by calling Waypoint’s connector with that student’s Bot key.

Sign in to the Waypoint account those bots should speak for (the live site is [waypoint-5o4r.onrender.com](https://waypoint-5o4r.onrender.com)), open **Connect your Bots**, and copy **Copy message with key**. In his Grok app, send that to the first bot, or paste the same values into a custom MCP server if Grok shows a Plugins or Connectors screen:

- **Name:** Waypoint
- **URL:** `https://waypoint-5o4r.onrender.com/mcp`
- **Header:** `Authorization: Bearer <that account’s Bot key>`

Then ask it to list the tools. A tool list means the connector is up. The key is what ties the bots to a person: Waypoint looks up the key and treats every tool call as that account. His Grok login does not choose the student.

He does not need to recreate the five bots if they already have their jobs. The first messages on that page are only for bots that do not exist yet. Those messages deliberately leave the key out so a bot can be shared as a template. The key belongs on the connector, not inside the bot’s instructions. If a bot says the connector is missing, he pastes the key in chat once and tells it not to save the key into instructions, a routine, or a template.

Two limits of running them on his personal Grok account:

- Every bot on that account shares one connector and one cloud computer. One key means they all read and write that one student’s Waypoint data. A second student needs their own Waypoint account and their own key, on a Grok account that is not already using the first key.
- Gmail, Google Calendar, and the case-portal sign-in are whatever is signed in on his Grok account. Texts, calendar events, and drafts will use those sign-ins.

**Check now** is optional. He tells the Manager to create a webhook routine, then pastes the webhook address and key back into section 3 on **Connect your Bots**. After that, **Check now** on the Brief wakes the Manager instead of running a simulation.

To confirm it, he tells the Manager to “run the night now.” Within a few minutes the Brief should show a time under each bot, and Activity lines that do not say simulated. The site has to be the public `https` address. A bot in the cloud cannot reach Waypoint running only on a laptop.
